texts.li: [lowtech] A hunting party of {FACTION} has followed a herd onto the colony's land. Their leader, {X_nameDef}, told {A_nameDef} they mean to camp {PLACE} until the herd moves on, and to take what game they need while it's here.

[!lowtech] A hunting party of {FACTION} has tracked game onto the colony's land, rifles slung and packs heavy. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll set up camp {PLACE} and stay until the hunting thins out.
Hunters of {FACTION} came through the trees this morning and stopped to look the land over. {X_nameDef} says the game here is too good to pass up. They are heading for a spot {PLACE} to make camp.

[winter] Hunters of {FACTION} have come down from the high country after the herds the snow pushed onto the colony's land. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} until the weather turns, and take only what they need.

[fall] It's the hunting season, and a party of {FACTION} has come onto the colony's land after the fall herds. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, politely enough, where the colony would rather they didn't shoot, and then pointed {PLACE} as the spot for their camp.

settled.li: The hunters from {FACTION} finished their camp {PLACE}: bedrolls around a fire, and a spot for dressing game.
[lowtech] The hunters from {FACTION} have a fire going {PLACE}, a rack for drying meat beside it, and their spears stacked against a tree.
[!lowtech] The hunters from {FACTION} have pitched their camp {PLACE}: bedrolls, a fire, and a gutting table they carried in on their backs.
The hunters from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}, with a fire low enough not to spook the game and a lookout in the nearest tree.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the hunters' camp has spent more evenings at the colony than at the camp fire lately. The colony feeds people better than the trail does, {X_pronoun} says, and {X_nameDef} would like to stay.
{X_nameDef}, the youngest of the hunters camped {PLACE}, has been helping the colony's cook with the butchering in the evenings, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay.
{X_nameDef}, who tracks for the hunters camped {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} is tired of following the herds and would rather stay where the herds come to {X_objective}.

farewell.li: The herd moved on, and the hunters from {FACTION} went with it. Their camp {PLACE} is packed up and gone, and the land is quieter.
The hunters from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} and moved on after the game, as hunters do.
The hunters from {FACTION} left before dawn, the way hunters do. All that's left {PLACE} is a ring of ash and a few bones.
The hunters from {FACTION} left a haunch of meat on the colony's gatepost by way of thanks, and went on after the herd.

lines.li: Whose turn is it to skin?

texts.li: A family of {FACTION} has come down the road with everything they own on their backs. Their home is gone, burned or taken, and {X_nameDef} would rather not say which. They ask only for a patch of ground {PLACE} to rest on for a while.

[lowtech] Refugees of {FACTION}, a family by the look of them, have stopped near the colony with a cart and a few bundles. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, politely, whether anyone would mind if they camped {PLACE} for a time.

[!lowtech] A family of {FACTION} has turned up on foot, carrying what they could save. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they need a few days, maybe longer, to work out where to go next, and they'll camp {PLACE} if the colony doesn't object.

[ws:hunger] {SITUATION} has emptied the farms of {FACTION}'s country, and a family of them has come as far as the colony on foot, thin as rails. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} until they know where they're going.

[ws:sickness] A family of {FACTION} has fled ahead of {SITUATION}, and every village on the road has turned them away for fear of it. {X_nameDef} swears none of them is sick, and asks only to camp {PLACE} a while, well apart from the colony.

[ws:war] A family of {FACTION}, driven out of their home by {SITUATION}, has come to the colony with a handcart and two goats. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} until it's safe to go back.

[ws:water] The water took their house in {SITUATION}, and a family of {FACTION} has walked up out of the valley with what they carried out of it. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a dry patch of ground {PLACE} to camp on.

[ws:drought] {SITUATION} dried up their well and then their fields, and a family of {FACTION} has given up and taken to the road. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} near the colony's water for a while.
[ws:weather] {SITUATION} drove a family of {FACTION} down out of the hills, half frozen. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a sheltered spot {PLACE} to camp until the worst of it passes.

[colony:Hospitable] A family of {FACTION} has come a long way on the word of strangers: the colony takes people in, they were told, and sees them on their way fed. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether it was true, and whether they might camp {PLACE} for a while.

settled.li: The family from {FACTION} put up a windbreak and laid out their beds around a fire {PLACE}. It almost looks like a home.
[winter] The family from {FACTION} has dug their camp into the lee of a bank {PLACE}, with every blanket they own around the fire.
The family from {FACTION} has their camp up {PLACE}. The children have already found the stream, and {X_nameDef} has hung the washing out on the windbreak.
The family from {FACTION} has their camp up {PLACE}, small and tidy, with a cookpot already on the fire and a line strung between two trees for the washing.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, came up to the colony this evening with a question {X_pronoun} has clearly been rehearsing. {X_nameDef} works hard, {X_pronoun} says, and would like to stay.

[ws:hunger|ws:sickness|ws:war|ws:water|ws:drought|ws:weather] {X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, says there's nothing left to go back to after {SITUATION}, and asks whether the colony would take {X_objective} in.
{X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, has been mending the colony's fences in the evenings without being asked. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether there might be a place to stay for good.

farewell.li: The family from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} and went on down the road. {X_nameDef} waved until the colony was out of sight.
The family from {FACTION} found somewhere to go, or decided to look for it. Their camp {PLACE} is empty now.
[ws:hunger|ws:sickness|ws:war|ws:water|ws:drought|ws:weather] The family from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} to go and see what {SITUATION} has left of their home.
The family from {FACTION} left their camp {PLACE} swept clean, with a little pile of firewood stacked for whoever comes next.

lines.li: Stay where I can see you.

texts.li: A band of prospectors of {FACTION} has come onto the colony's land with picks, pans and a lot of confidence. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} there's ore in this ground, and they mean to camp {PLACE} until they find it.

[lowtech] Prospectors of {FACTION} have arrived with mules' worth of tools on their own backs. {X_nameDef} says an old map brought them here. They will camp {PLACE} and dig, and they'll sell whatever they find.

[!lowtech] Prospectors of {FACTION} have turned up with sample bags and a battered ground scanner that {X_nameDef} swears still works. They plan to camp {PLACE} and dig test holes until they hit something.

[ws:rush] {SITUATION} has every prospector in the region out with a pan, and a band of {FACTION}'s has decided the colony's hills are worth a look. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} and dig, and sell whatever they find.

settled.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} finished their camp {PLACE}, with a windbreak against the weather and a torch to dig by.
The prospectors' camp {PLACE} is up, and the first test holes are already dug in a neat line toward the hills.
The prospectors from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with sieves stacked by the fire and a hand-drawn map pinned under a rock.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the prospectors' camp is tired of digging holes for other people's fortunes, and asks whether the colony could use a steady pair of hands.
{X_nameDef} from the prospectors {PLACE} says the only thing worth finding round here is the colony, and asks, only half joking, whether there's a place for {X_objective} in it.
{X_nameDef}, the prospectors' cook, says {X_pronoun} has dug enough empty holes for one lifetime and would rather cook for people who stay in one place.

farewell.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} filled in their last holes, packed up their camp {PLACE} and moved on, still sure the big find is over the next hill.
The prospectors from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} and left, arguing about where to dig next.
The prospectors from {FACTION} packed up {PLACE} and left, a little richer or a little poorer, depending on which of them you ask.

lines.li: There's a seam here, I can feel it.

texts.li: Pilgrims of {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land to rest. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, told {A_nameDef} their road is long and their feet are sore, and they'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few days before they go on.

A small band of pilgrims of {FACTION} is walking toward a holy place far from here. They've asked to rest {PLACE} for a few days, to pray and mend their sandals. {X_nameDef} promises they'll take very little.

[ideology] Pilgrims of {IDEO} from {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land on their way to a shrine of their ideoligion. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to rest {PLACE} a few days, and to keep their prayers there.

[ideology,sameFaith] Pilgrims of {FACTION} who keep {IDEO}, the colony's own ideoligion, have stopped to rest among their own. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few days before going on to the shrine.
[ws:faith] {SITUATION} has put pilgrims on every road in the region, and a band of {FACTION}'s has stopped by the colony to rest. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE}.

[winter] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have come through the snow on their way to a holy place, and stopped at the colony because they could go no further today. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} until the road clears.

[colony:Devout] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have turned off their road to rest at the colony: they had heard on the way that it keeps its faith, and wanted to see it for themselves. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} a few days.

settled.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} made a simple camp {PLACE}, with a place set aside for prayer.
[ideology] The pilgrims of {IDEO} have made their camp {PLACE}, with a shrine of piled stones at the edge of camp for their evening prayers.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} have laid out their bedrolls {PLACE} in a careful ring, and they sing before they eat.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the pilgrims camped {PLACE}, says the road has given {X_objective} what {X_pronoun} came for, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay with the colony instead of walking on.
[sameFaith] {X_nameDef}, one of the pilgrims {PLACE}, has found people of {X_possessive} own ideoligion at the colony, and asks to end the pilgrimage here.
{X_nameDef}, who has walked with the pilgrims camped {PLACE} since the start of their road, says {X_pronoun} feels {X_pronoun} has arrived somewhere, and would like to stay.

farewell.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} rested, prayed, and went on their way. {X_nameDef} said they'd remember the colony in their prayers.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} at dawn and walked on toward their holy place.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} left at first light, singing quietly so as not to wake the colony. Most of the colony was already up.

lines.li: Mind your feet, they're all you have.
Bless the ones who let us rest.

texts.li: Traders of {FACTION} have decided the colony is worth more than a day's visit. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll set up a stall {PLACE} and stay a few days, and anyone with silver is welcome.

[lowtech] A small band of traders of {FACTION} has stopped on the colony's land with packs full of goods. They mean to put up a stall {PLACE} and sell to the colony for a few days, the way market folk do.
[!lowtech] Traders of {FACTION} have arrived with packs, a folding table and a hand-painted sign. {X_nameDef} says they'll camp {PLACE} and keep the stall open for a few days.

[ws:trade|ws:road] With {SITUATION} bringing more traffic past the colony than ever, traders of {FACTION} have decided to stop and sell to it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll put up a stall {PLACE} for a few days.

settled.li: The traders from {FACTION} have their stall up {PLACE}, with a torch to see the goods by.
The traders' stall {PLACE} is open for business, with the best of the goods at the front and a sign promising fair prices, which {A_nameDef} doubts.
The traders from {FACTION} have laid their goods out on blankets {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} is already calling out prices to anyone in earshot.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who carries the traders' packs, has had enough of the road, and asks whether the colony would take on someone who can count and lift.
{X_nameDef} from the traders' stall {PLACE} says the colony is the best market on the road, and would like to stop moving and be part of it.
{X_nameDef}, who keeps the traders' accounts, has decided the colony needs someone who can tell a fair price from a bad one, and would like to be that someone.

farewell.li: The traders from {FACTION} packed their stall and moved on to the next settlement.
Business was what it was. The traders from {FACTION} folded up their stall {PLACE} and left.
The traders from {FACTION} packed up their stall {PLACE}, counted their silver twice and went on, promising to be back when the roads are good.

lines.li: Fair prices, best on the road!
I'll throw in the bag for free.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a traveling smith of {FACTION}, has come onto the colony's land with helpers and a cart of tools. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} for a few days, sell what they've made, and mend what they can.

[medieval] A smith of {FACTION} has stopped near the colony with an anvil on a cart and apprentices to push it. {X_nameDef} means to camp {PLACE}, burn some charcoal and sell blades and mail to anyone who can pay.

[industrial] {X_nameDef}, a smith of {FACTION}, travels with a portable forge on a handcart and a sack of coke. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} for a few days, fix whatever the colony brings them, and sell the rest.

[winter] A smith of {FACTION} has come in out of the cold, glad of an excuse to light a forge. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} until the weather turns, and mend whatever the winter has broken.

settled.li: The smith from {FACTION} set up a work spot and a table of wares at the camp {PLACE}. The ringing of a hammer carries all the way to the colony.
The smith's camp {PLACE} is up and the forge is lit. There's already a queue of colonists with bent tools pretending to just be passing.
The smith from {FACTION} has a fire going hot {PLACE} and a row of half-finished blades cooling on a flat stone.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who has been working the smith's bellows, wants to stop moving, and asks whether the colony needs someone who knows metal.
{X_nameDef} from the smith's camp {PLACE} has been eyeing the colony's workshop for days, and finally asked whether {X_pronoun} might work in it, for good.
{X_nameDef}, the smith's apprentice, has been watching the colony's crafters work and thinks {X_pronoun} could learn more here than on the road. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.

farewell.li: The smith from {FACTION} loaded the cart and moved on, the anvil ringing faintly over every bump in the road.
The smith's camp {PLACE} is gone, and the forge with it. The colony's tools have never been sharper.
The smith from {FACTION} put out the forge {PLACE}, packed the anvil and left a fixed hinge on the colony's gate without saying a word about it.

texts.li: A hermit called {X_nameDef}, once of {FACTION}, has walked onto the colony's land and started pacing out a spot {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, in very few words, that {X_pronoun} means to build a hut and stay the season.
{X_nameDef}, a hermit who left {FACTION} years ago, has chosen a spot {PLACE} to build a hut for the season. {X_nameDef} asks nothing of the colony and seems to hope the colony will ask nothing back.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a hermit of {FACTION}, has come down out of the snow line, where even hermits can't stay in this weather. {X_nameDef} means to build a hut {PLACE} and wait the winter out, and would rather not be visited.

{X_nameDef} turned up {PLACE} with an axe, a sack and a goat, and started cutting poles without asking anyone. When {A_nameDef} went over to see, {X_nameDef}, once of {FACTION}, said only that {X_pronoun} would be gone by the end of the season.

settled.li: {X_nameDef} finished a small hut {PLACE}, with a door, a roof and a fire outside it.
{X_nameDef}'s hut {PLACE} is finished: crooked, small and very solid. Smoke comes out of the roof in the mornings.
{X_nameDef} has a hut up {PLACE}, and a little garden fenced off beside it with sticks and twine.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the hermit camped {PLACE}, came to the colony's door this evening. After a long silence, {X_pronoun} asked whether there might be room for one more.
{X_nameDef}, the hermit {PLACE}, has been leaving firewood at the colony's gate every morning for a week. Today {X_nameDef} knocked, and asked to come in for good.
{X_nameDef}, the hermit {PLACE}, came to the colony's fire one cold night and didn't leave when it burned down. In the morning {X_pronoun} asked to stay.

farewell.li: {X_nameDef} shut the door of the hut {PLACE} one last time and walked off without looking back. The hut is the colony's now, if it wants it.
The hermit's hut {PLACE} is empty. {X_nameDef} left in the night without a word, which is how {X_nameDef} arrived.
{X_nameDef} is gone from the hut {PLACE}. A carved bird was left on the colony's gatepost, which may have been a goodbye.
